n: A summary heading: these are the terms of a covenant made in Moab, renewing and adding to the one made at Sinai (Horeb) forty years earlier. (In Hebrew Bibles this verse closes chapter 28.)

f.w: in the land of Moab
f.g: The plains east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.

f.w: Horeb

n: Moses calls all Israel together and appeals to what they had seen with their own eyes in Egypt.

f.w: Ye have seen

n: They had witnessed the plagues and miracles.

f.w: temptations
f.g: Here “trials” or “tests” — the plagues that tested Pharaoh.

n: A sobering admission: despite all they’d seen, they still lacked true understanding. Spiritual sight is a gift that must be sought.

f.w: an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear

n: Moses now voices God’s own words: for forty years their clothes and sandals never wore out.

f.w: your clothes are not waxen old upon you
waxen old

n: They lived without ordinary bread and wine, relying on manna, so they would learn to know the Lord as their sustainer.

f.w: Ye have not eaten bread

n: God gave them victory over the Amorite kings Sihon and Og east of the Jordan.

f.w: Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan

n: That land became the inheritance of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.

f.w: the half tribe of Manasseh

n: So keep this covenant and prosper. Covenant faithfulness and true success go together.

f.w: that ye may prosper

n: Everyone stands before God today — leaders and ordinary people alike.

f.w: Ye stand this day all of you
f.g: The whole nation assembled as one.

n: Even children, wives, and foreigners serving in the camp — down to the woodcutters and water carriers — are included in the covenant.

f.w: from the hewer of thy wood unto the drawer of thy water

n: The purpose: to enter a covenant sealed by an oath with the Lord.

f.w: enter into covenant
f.g: Literally “pass into” the covenant — perhaps recalling walking between sacrificial pieces (Genesis 15:17).

n: Through it Israel becomes God’s people and he becomes their God — the heart of every covenant, promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

f.w: that he may be unto thee a God

n: This covenant is not only for the people present.

f.w: Neither with you only

n: It includes future generations not yet born — and, by extension, all who would later join Israel through covenant.

f.w: him that is not here with us this day

n: Moses reminds them of their experiences living in Egypt and passing through other nations.

f.w: how we came through the nations

n: They had seen the idols of those peoples — lifeless objects of wood, stone, silver, and gold.

f.w: their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold

n: A warning about any person, family, or tribe turning away. Like a poisonous root, one person’s apostasy can spread bitterness through the community.

f.w: a root that beareth gall and wormwood
f.g: Gall and wormwood = bitter, poisonous plants.

n: The danger of false security: someone hears the curses but tells himself, “I’ll be fine, even if I do what I want.” Self-deception sweeps away the whole.

f.w: bless himself in his heart
to add drunkenness to thirst
f.g: An idiom, perhaps “to sweep away the watered with the dry” — ruin everything.

n: God will not overlook such a person. His jealous anger — protective love for his covenant — will burn against him, and his name will be erased.

f.w: jealousy
f.g: God’s zeal for an exclusive covenant relationship.

f.w: blot out his name

n: That person would be singled out for judgment from among all the tribes.

f.w: separate him unto evil

n: Future generations and foreigners would see the ruined land and ask what happened.

f.w: the stranger that shall come from a far land

n: The land would look like Sodom and Gomorrah — burned, salty, barren. Admah and Zeboiim were sister cities destroyed with them.

f.w: the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim
brimstone

n: Nations would ask why God poured out such anger on his own land.

f.w: Wherefore hath the LORD done thus

n: The answer: they abandoned the covenant God made with them at the Exodus.

f.w: forsaken the covenant

n: They worshiped gods they had no relationship with — gods that had never done anything for them.

f.w: whom he had not given unto them
f.g: Gods not assigned to them — Israel’s portion was the Lord alone (Deuteronomy 32:8-9).

n: So all the written curses fell upon the land.

f.w: all the curses that are written in this book

n: God uprooted them and cast them into another land — a prophetic description of exile. The phrase “as it is this day” speaks from the perspective of those who later lived it.

f.w: rooted them out of their land

n: A beloved verse: some things only God knows, but what he has revealed belongs to us and our children — so we can live it. Latter-day Saints treasure continuing revelation.

f.w: The secret things belong unto the LORD our God
